abstract: Music source separation extracts vocals and instruments from a mixed recording, enabling remixing, content production, and music analysis. Existing systems commonly operate on waveforms or full-band spectrograms. Waveform inputs contain many samples even in short segments, whereas a single spectrogram resolution imposes a shared time–frequency resolution trade-off across frequency ranges. We propose SubRoFormer, a Transformer-based system comprising a subband module and a residual RoFormer module. The subband module decomposes the mixture into frequency-localized, lower-rate signals for separation. It then reconstructs the target waveforms from the estimated subbands. The residual RoFormer module models temporal and cross-band relationships on temporally compressed features. It combines this context with fine-rate features through gated residual fusion to estimate source-specific complex masks. On the MUSDB18-HQ test set, training only on MUSDB18-HQ yields an average signal-to-distortion ratio (SDR) of 10.63 dB across four stems using target-specific models, achieving state-of-the-art performance among the compared systems without extra training data. With 500 additional training songs, a single model jointly separating all four stems achieves an average SDR of 11.59 dB, establishing state-of-the-art performance among the compared single-model multi-stem systems trained with extra data. Code and checkpoints are released at https://github.com/ArchiMickey/SubRoformer.

sections.body: The introduction states that existing systems use waveforms or full-band spectrograms, where a single spectrogram resolution fixes one time-frequency trade-off across frequency ranges. The paper studies a channel-wise subband analysis that filters and downsamples the waveform before computing local spectra, paired with a separator that predicts masks on a fine temporal grid and models longer context on a shorter sequence. Three contributions are listed: a fixed subband time-domain representation with a quantified reconstruction distortion, a polyphase implementation, and SubRoFormer. The stated comparisons summarize reported systems and do not isolate architectural effects under matched training conditions.
sections.heading: Introduction
sections.headline: Subband frontend plus a residual RoFormer separator targets the time-frequency trade-off in music source separation.

sections.body: The related-work section groups music source separation systems into time-domain, hybrid, time-frequency-domain, and subband or nonuniform representations. It gives the additive mixing model and the complex-mask formulation used in the time-frequency family. It notes that prior channel-wise subband systems such as CWS-PResUNet and XUMX-SliCQ use uniform bands or variable-resolution transforms, which limit adaptation of frequency resolution across spectral regions. Figure 1 in this section gives the overall pipeline, with a fixed front end producing decimated subbands, fine-rate boundary blocks and a temporally patched axial RoFormer, and an inverse path that resynthesizes the stems.
sections.heading: Related Work
sections.headline: Prior systems span waveform, hybrid, spectrogram, and subband separators, and the paper positions itself among them.

sections.body: The subband representation uses a triangular filter bank of FIR filters built with a Hamming window, followed by analytic conversion, complex demodulation, and decimation. Synthesis reverses these steps by interpolation, remodulation, real-part projection, and band summation. Table I reports reconstruction SDR, LSD, NME, and rate on MUSDB18-HQ, and the paper states that the mel-linear and ERB-linear banks show lower reconstruction SDR than the STFT, MDCT, and Haar controls, which reconstruct near-perfectly. A polyphase implementation reduces the complexity of the analysis and synthesis from O(KNL) to O(K L/D log L/D) by avoiding discarded samples and zero-filled sequences.
sections.heading: Subband Time-Domain Representation
sections.headline: A fixed triangular subband filter bank with polyphase implementation reconstructs the mixture with measured distortion.

sections.body: Each subband is transformed with a local STFT, and a preprocessing block refines fine-rate features while retaining a skip representation. A learned patchification groups neighboring temporal frames before stacked axial RoFormer blocks that alternate subband-axis and temporal-axis Transformers with rotary positional embeddings. The patched features are unpatchified and concatenated with the skip features, then combined by a gated fusion module (GEGLU) that adds a gated projection to the coarse output. A postprocessing block predicts complex masks applied to the mixture spectra, and the multi-stem variant uses separate output heads on a shared backbone. Training combines a waveform L1 term with multi-resolution complex-STFT errors summed over five window sizes.
sections.heading: Residual SubRoFormer
sections.headline: SubRoFormer combines fine-rate features, a patched axial RoFormer, and gated residual fusion to predict complex masks.

sections.body: Main comparisons train on the 100 MUSDB18-HQ training songs with the augmentation policy from ZFTurbo's Music-Source-Separation-Training, and evaluate SDR with museval on 50 test tracks. Stem scores are medians over tracks, and the four-stem mean is the arithmetic mean of the stem scores. SubRoFormer-S has 22.52M parameters and SubRoFormer-B has 97.17M in single-stem form, and both are trained for one million optimizer updates on MUSDB18-HQ-only data. Table II lists baselines with their parameter counts and per-stem SDR values, and Figure 4 plots mean SDR against total deployed parameters. The commercial ACE Studio result is included only as context, since its training data and parameter count are unknown.
sections.heading: Experiments
sections.headline: Experiments use MUSDB18-HQ with SDR as the primary metric, and training data and augmentation are described.

sections.body: The four-stem average of 10.63 dB is reported as 0.61 dB above the strongest complete author-reported public-data BS-RoFormer result and 0.99 dB above the public-data Mel-RoFormer result. BS-RoFormer keeps a 1.38 dB advantage on bass. A separate vocals-only study finds two global-STFT replacements score below the 10.88 dB reference, and temporal patch factors one and two score 11.02 and 10.94 dB. The authors state these are single-seed observations and not causal. Repeated seeds, efficiency measurements, and parameter-matched all-stem ablations are listed as required before the result can be treated as a firm claim.
sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.headline: SubRoFormer-B reaches 10.63 dB on MUSDB18-HQ without extra data, but the authors call the evidence preliminary.
